meaning.text: Ralston renders the name Polunochnitsas as "Midnight Sisters".

behavior_habitat.text: In the Government of Archangel, tradition tells of twelve midnight sisters.
They force the children to cry out with pain.
Afanasyev names them alongside the poludnitsy, as known in the Archangel Government.

rationale.text: Afanasyev records the twelve midnight sisters for the Archangel Government only, citing the Archangel provincial year-book for 1864.
Ralston's passage on the Twelve Midnight Sisters cites Afanasief, P. V. S. iii. 77 (with Buslaev), so it counts with Afanasyev, not as an independent source.
The verified entry names one people (Russians) and every surviving clause rests on one 19th-century compiler, Afanasyev, so the grade is literary.

notes.text: appearance: no source describes the polunochnitsy's body, dress or form; both pages say only that there are twelve sisters. Searched polunochnitsa, polunochnitsas, poluno, "midnight sisters", "midnight spirit", midnight, полуночница, полуночницы, полуночниц, полуночн, полунош, шмар, шмары across all sources.
dealing_with_it: no ward, offering or remedy against the polunochnitsy is given on either page (ralston1872 p.148, afanasyev1869 p.77); same searches as for appearance.
origin: neither page says where the polunochnitsy come from or who becomes one; same searches as for appearance.
variants: both pages give only the Archangel Government tradition; no regional or people variant exists in the corpus hits.

family: the hints file proposes field, but no opened page places the polunochnitsy in fields. afanasyev1869 p.77 sets them in a passage on ailments (the falling sickness, klikushestvo) and says they attack children and make them cry with pain, which supports disease-and-fate; recorded that instead.
